title:
STATIC PROTECTION
RELAYS
text:
If one moment captured the spirit of 1965, it was arguably Bob Dylan's decision to "go electric" at the Newport Folk Festival, a symbolic sign that culture was entering a new technological era. That same year we introduced our first static protection relays that replaced moving parts with solid-state electronics. They were faster, smaller, and more reliable than anything seen before.

Originally made in Helsinki, relay production started up in Vaasa in 1967. Across music and industry, electronics were replacing mechanics, and we were part of it.
funFact: The Vaasa factories were also producing fire and gas alarms, stoves, and light controls during the ‘60s. A little later we would even make a disco light system.
